text: What is the mass ratio of ethylene glycol ($\mathrm{C}_{2}\mathrm{H}_{6}\mathrm{O}_{2}$, molar mass = 62 g/mol) required for making 500 g of 0.25 molal aqueous solution and 250 mL of 0.25 molar aqueous solution?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 25th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Molality is moles of solute per kg of solvent, and $500\text{g}$ is the mass of the whole solution. Let the molal solution contain $n$ mol of glycol: mass of glycol $=62n\text{g}$ and mass of water $=(500-62n)\text{g}$.

$0.25=\dfrac{n}{(500-62n)/1000}\Rightarrow 1000n=125-15.5n\Rightarrow n=0.1231\text{mol}$

$w_{1}=62\times 0.1231=7.63\text{g}$

For $250\text{mL}$ of $0.25\text{M}$ solution, moles $=0.25\times 0.250=0.0625\text{mol}$, so $w_{2}=62\times 0.0625=3.875\text{g}$.

$\dfrac{w_{1}}{w_{2}}=\dfrac{7.63}{3.875}=1.97\approx 2$

So the mass ratio is $2:1$.

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 25th January Evening Shift

Find out the major product from the following reaction.


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 25th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Concentrated $\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{SO}{}_{4}$ protonates the –OH of 2,2,6-trimethylcyclohexan-1-ol, and loss of water gives a secondary carbocation at C-1.

C-1 lies between C-2, which carries two $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$ groups, and C-6, which carries one $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$ and one H. A 1,2-methyl shift from C-2 gives a tertiary cation at C-2; a 1,2-hydride shift from C-6 gives a tertiary cation at C-6.


[IMG]

The C-6 cation can lose a proton only to form trisubstituted alkenes (C-1=C-6 or C-5=C-6, options A and B). The C-2 cation loses the H on C-1 to form 1,2,3-trimethylcyclohex-1-ene, a tetrasubstituted alkene.

In hot concentrated acid the protonation, shift and deprotonation steps are reversible, so the alkenes equilibrate and the most substituted, most stable alkene is the major product.

Hence, the correct option is (D).

text: The isomeric deuterated bromide with molecular formula $\mathrm{C}_{4}\mathrm{H}_{8}\mathrm{DBr}$ having two chiral carbon atoms is
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 25th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
A carbon atom is chiral when it carries four different groups.

(A) 2-Bromo-1-deuterobutane, $\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{D}-\mathrm{CHBr}-\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$: only C2 (H, Br, $\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{D}$, $\mathrm{C}{}_{2}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}$) is chiral; C1 carries two H atoms.

(B) 2-Bromo-1-deutero-2-methylpropane, $\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{D}-\mathrm{CBr}(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}){}_{2}$: C2 carries two $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$ groups, so there is no chiral carbon.

(C) 2-Bromo-3-deuterobutane, $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}-\mathrm{CHBr}-\mathrm{CHD}-\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$: C2 (H, Br, $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$, $\mathrm{CHDCH}{}_{3}$) and C3 (H, D, $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$, $\mathrm{CHBrCH}{}_{3}$) are both chiral.

(D) 2-Bromo-2-deuterobutane, $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}-\mathrm{CDBr}-\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$: only C2 (D, Br, $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$, $\mathrm{C}{}_{2}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}$) is chiral.

Hence, the correct option is (C).

solution.body:
A. Propan-1-amine, $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{NH}{}_{2}$, is a primary amine and N-methylethanamine, $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{NHCH}{}_{3}$, is a secondary amine; the functional groups differ, so they are functional isomers: III.

B. Hexan-2-one ($\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{COC}{}_{4}\mathrm{H}{}_{9}$) and hexan-3-one ($\mathrm{C}{}_{2}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}\mathrm{COC}{}_{3}\mathrm{H}{}_{7}$) have the same functional group with different alkyl groups on its two sides, so they are metamers: I.

C. Ethanamide, $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{CONH}{}_{2}$, and hydroxyethanimine, $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{OH})=\mathrm{NH}$, differ only in the position of one H atom and the double bond and interconvert, so they are tautomers: IV.

D. o-Nitrophenol and p-nitrophenol differ only in the position of $-\mathrm{NO}{}_{2}$ on the ring, so they are positional isomers: II.

The pair in B could loosely be called position isomers too, but metamerism is the specific term for unequal alkyl groups on the two sides of the same group, and only option (A) fits the other three matches.

Hence, the correct option is (A).

text:
The number of pairs of the solutions having the same value of the osmotic pressure from the following is $_________$.

(Assume 100% ionization)

A. 0.500 $\mathrm{M}\mathrm{C}_{2}\mathrm{H}_{5}\mathrm{OH}(\mathrm{aq})$ and 0.25 $\mathrm{M}\mathrm{KBr}(\mathrm{aq})$

B. 0.100 $\mathrm{M}\mathrm{K}_{4}[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_{6}](\mathrm{aq})$ and 0.100 $\mathrm{M}\mathrm{FeSO}_{4}(\mathrm{NH}_{4})_{2}\mathrm{SO}_{4}(\mathrm{aq})$

C. 0.05 $\mathrm{M}\mathrm{K}_{4}[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_{6}](\mathrm{aq})$ and 0.25 $\mathrm{M}\mathrm{NaCl}(\mathrm{aq})$

D. 0.15 $\mathrm{M}\mathrm{NaCl}(\mathrm{aq})$ and 0.1 $\mathrm{M}\mathrm{BaCl}_{2}(\mathrm{aq})$

E. 0.02 $\mathrm{M}\mathrm{KCl}.\mathrm{MgCl}_{2}.6\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}(\mathrm{aq})$ and 0.05 $\mathrm{M}\mathrm{KCl}(\mathrm{aq})$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 25th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Osmotic pressure is $π=iCRT$, so two solutions have equal $π$ when $iC$ is equal (100% ionisation).

A: $\mathrm{C}{}_{2}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}\mathrm{OH}$ is a non-electrolyte, $iC=1\times 0.500=0.50$; $\mathrm{KBr}$ ($\mathrm{K}{}^{+}+\mathrm{Br}{}^{-}$), $iC=2\times 0.25=0.50$. Equal.

B: $\mathrm{K}{}_{4}[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN}){}_{6}]$ ($4~\mathrm{K}{}^{+}\qquad +[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN}){}_{6}]{}^{4-}$), $iC=5\times 0.100=0.50$; Mohr's salt $\mathrm{FeSO}{}_{4}\cdot (\mathrm{NH}{}_{4}){}_{2}\mathrm{SO}{}_{4}$ ($\mathrm{Fe}{}^{2+}\qquad +2\mathrm{NH}{}_{4}{}^{+}+2\mathrm{SO}{}_{4}{}^{2-}$), $iC=5\times 0.100=0.50$. Equal.

C: $\mathrm{K}{}_{4}[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN}){}_{6}]$, $iC=5\times 0.05=0.25$; $\mathrm{NaCl}$, $iC=2\times 0.25=0.50$. Not equal.

D: $\mathrm{NaCl}$, $iC=2\times 0.15=0.30$; $\mathrm{BaCl}{}_{2}$ ($\mathrm{Ba}{}^{2+}+2\mathrm{Cl}{}^{-}$), $iC=3\times 0.1=0.30$. Equal.

E: carnallite $\mathrm{KCl}\cdot \mathrm{MgCl}{}_{2}\cdot 6\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}$ ($\mathrm{K}{}^{+}+\mathrm{Mg}{}^{2+}+3\mathrm{Cl}{}^{-}$), $iC=5\times 0.02=0.10$; $\mathrm{KCl}$, $iC=2\times 0.05=0.10$. Equal.

The pairs A, B, D and E have equal osmotic pressure.

Hence, the answer is 4.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 25th January Evening Shift

text:
A first order reaction has the rate constant, $\mathrm{k}=4.6\times 10^{-3}\mathrm{s}^{-1}$. The number of correct statement/s from the following is/are $__________$

Given : $\log 3=0.48$

A. Reaction completes in 1000 s.

B. The reaction has a half-life of 500 s.

C. The time required for 10% completion is 25 times the time required for 90% completion.

D. The degree of dissociation is equal to ($1-\mathrm{e}^{-\mathrm{kt}}$)

E. The rate and the rate constant have the same unit.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 25th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
(A) $\mathrm{A}_{1-α}⟶$ Products

$\mathrm{k}=4.6\times 10^{-3}\mathrm{s}^{-1}$

$\mathrm{kt}=\ln \frac{1}{1-α}$

$α=1-\mathrm{e}^{-\mathrm{kt}}$

Reaction completes at infinite time.

(B) For first order reaction,

Half-life $=\frac{0.693}{4.6\times 10^{-3}}=150.65\mathrm{s}$

(C) For $10%$ completion, $t=t_{1}$

$\begin{array}{l} a=100,a-x=100-10=90 \\  \\ k=\dfrac{2.303}{t_{1}}\log \dfrac{100}{90}=4.6\times 10^{-3} \\  \\ t_{1}=\dfrac{2.303}{4.6\times 10^{-3}}\times 0.04575 \end{array}$

For $90%$ completion $t=t_{2},a=100,a-x=100-90=10$

$\begin{array}{l} k=\dfrac{2.303}{t_{2}}\log \dfrac{100}{10}=4.6\times 10^{-3} \\  \\ \dfrac{2.303}{t_{2}}\times 1=4.6\times 10^{-3}\Rightarrow t_{2}=\dfrac{2.303}{4.6\times 10^{-3}} \\  \\ \dfrac{t_{2}}{t_{1}}=\dfrac{1}{0.04575}=21.85\text{(Incorrect)} \end{array}$

(E) Unit of rate = mol $L^{–1}s^{–1}$

Unit of rate constant $= s^{–1}$

Both have different units.

$\therefore$ Number of correct statements $=1$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 25th January Evening Shift

solution.body:
Ceric ammonium nitrate gives a red colour only with alcohols, and the iodoform test needs a $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{CO}{}^{-}$ group or a $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{OH}){}^{-}$ group that can be oxidised to it.

Acetophenone and acetaldehyde give the iodoform test but have no $-\mathrm{OH}$, so they give no red colour with ceric ammonium nitrate; ethyl methyl ether gives neither test.

2-Phenylethanol, $\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{OH}$, is a primary alcohol without a $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{OH}){}^{-}$ unit, and 2-cyclohexylpropan-2-ol is a tertiary alcohol that cannot be oxidised to a methyl ketone; both give the red colour but not the iodoform test.

1-Phenylpropan-2-ol, butan-2-ol and 1-cyclohexylpropan-2-ol are alcohols containing $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{OH}){}^{-}$, so they give both tests:


[IMG]

Hence, the answer is 3.
